notes.claim: A transistor in its linear region dissipates far more power (6 V at 100 mA, 600 mW) than the same transistor used as a switch (tens of milliwatts or less).
A switch that is closed has zero voltage across it and so no power loss.
A switch that is fully on or fully off dissipates little heat while controlling load power.
An IGBT should not be run in linear mode, because that causes excessive conduction losses.
Switching losses in an IGBT and its diode are the product of the switching energies and the switching frequency.
For i4: a power BJT with a gain of 20 needs at least 5 A of base current to pass 100 A, a burden for its control circuit.
For i4: the IGBT's cost against a BJT is a slower turn-off.
For i4: many devices already carry a freewheeling path, so an added diode is not always needed.
